title: Randomized reservoir sampling for KV reuse and decode fairness
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Problem: The paged KV cache shows hotspotting where a small set of segments remains resident and repeatedly serviced by the same kernels, causing decode unfairness and thrashing for lower-priority streams. Deterministic reclamation and strict LRU increases fragmentation and can exacerbate tail latency when many concurrent sessions prefill overlapping token spans. Goal: Design and prototype an allocation+reuse policy that reduces long-lived hotspot dominance, improves tail decode fairness, and keeps overall prefill latency within SLOs. Approach: we will implement a randomized reservoir-sampling based candidate set across KV slots combined with an occupancy thermostat. The sampler maintains a small, weighted reservoir per shard that probabilistically favors recently touched but underutilized segments (weight = f(recency, touch_count, tenant_weight, estimated_decode_cost)). On eviction/compaction windows, the reservoir nominates candidates for reuse or compaction instead of purely LRU-based choices. The thermostat monitors decode wave metrics and the kernel handshake queue to throttle prefill bursts (soft backpressure) and trigger lightweight re-ranking of reservoir weights to prefer segments that unblock multiple pending decodes. Key deliverables: 1) prototype reservoir sampler and weight function, 2) occupancy thermostat implementation and kernel-handshake integration, 3) metrics/dashboard and ablation tests vs LRU and current hybrid allocator.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test that reservoir sampler can nominate candidates under synthetic load and reproduce selection distribution statistics
End-to-end benchmark that reduces 95th percentile per-request prefill latency by >= 10% on mixed tenant load compared to baseline allocator
No regression in median latency or token throughput (within 2%)
Observed reduction in slot churn and fragment creation rate on long-running workload traces
Dashboard charts for reservoir size, nomination rate, thermostat throttle percent, and kernel-handshake queue length available in Console dev project
design_notes: Reservoir per shard kept small (32 entries) to limit memory and CPU overhead; entries carry a 32-bit fingerprint and weight metric
Weight function design: w = alpha*recency_score + beta*(1 / (1+touch_count)) + gamma*tenant_priority - delta*estimated_decode_cost
Sampling should use reservoir sampling with exponential decay to adapt to temporal shifts without full rescans
Thermostat is not a hard limiter: it produces a soft throttle factor [0,1] applied to prefill admission and a re-ranking boost for reservoir entries that unblock multiple queued decodes
Kernel handshake integration: expose a micro-protocol where kernels advertise available concurrency windows and the thermostat uses a lightweight probe to avoid saturating kernels with large prefills
Safety: when memory pressure is acute, fall back to existing eviction policy deterministically to avoid data-structure maintenance costs during OOM events
Security: no tenant affinity data beyond tenant id used for weighting; no cross-tenant KV visibility
implementation_plan: M1 (2 days): Add lightweight reservoir data structure to KV shard metadata and unit tests for insert/evict/sample behavior
M2 (3 days): Implement weight function and periodic decay job; add telemetry counters for nomination and selection
M3 (4 days): Integrate thermostat that observes kernel-handshake queue length and decode latency histograms; expose throttle API
M4 (3 days): Wire nomination into compaction/eviction path with staged rollout flag: off -> canary (10%) -> ramp
M5 (2 days): Add end-to-end benchmarking harness and console panels for new metrics
M6 (2 days): Run 72h soak test on dedicated cluster with mixed workload traces and tune hyperparams
M7 (1 day): Documentation, PR, and postmortem template for rollout
testing_and_metrics: Unit tests: reservoir invariants, decay behavior, thermostat backpressure math
Integration: simulated multi-tenant prefill workload with synthetic hotspots to validate selection distribution
Perf benchmark: run standard paged-attention benchmark suite measuring p50/p95/p99 prefill and decode latencies, token throughput, and GPU utilization
Regression tests: memory usage under heavy GC, compaction correctness
Key metrics to monitor: nomination_rate, selection_entropy, fragment_creation_per_minute, prefill_admit_rate, thermostat_throttle_pct, kernel_handshake_wait_ms
Ablation studies: disable decay vs enable, vary reservoir size (8/32/128), vary thermostat sensitivity to kernel queue length
